title: Chemicals in Household and Personal Care Products
seo_title: Grade 11 General Science: Chemicals in Household and Personal Care Products Worksheets
standard_code: Grade 11 General Science, Term 1: Physics and chemistry in daily life
standard_text: Application of chemical substances in household and personal care products: acids and bases, soaps and detergents, cleaners, cosmetics; reading product labels; safe use, storage and disposal. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, General Science, Term 1)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 General Science worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Term 1): acids and bases at home, soaps and detergents, cleaners, labels and hazard symbols, and safe use. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Read the label before you use a product.
key_sub: Never mix bleach with other cleaners.
body_html:
How to think about it

Many household products are acids or bases: vinegar and calamansi juice are acidic; soap, baking soda and drain cleaner are basic. Soap and detergent molecules have a water-loving end and an oil-loving end, so they lift grease and dirt into water.

Labels list ingredients, hazards (flammable, corrosive, toxic) and safe use. Mixing bleach with vinegar or ammonia releases toxic gases. Store chemicals in their original containers, away from children, and dispose of them properly to protect water and soil.

Example

Is vinegar acidic or basic?

Sour taste

Answer: acidic

Example

Why can phosphate detergents harm lakes?

Too many nutrients

Answer: they cause algal blooms (eutrophication)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking natural products are always safe.
  • Mixing cleaning products to make them stronger.
  • Storing chemicals in drink bottles.

items.q: The ocean absorbs more CO₂ from the air. What happens to ocean pH?

items.e: More H⁺ ions → lower pH. Since 1750, surface ocean pH fell from about 8.2 to 8.1.
